A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SafeAuto and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original BDD-X and DriveLM evaluations, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, traffic-rule violation measurements, and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations and analyses and additionally reports TimeLLM results in the BDD-X control-prediction comparison.

M1.justification: The PDCE loss, MLN verification and re-prompting procedure, and multimodal retrieval model are unchanged. Sections 3 and Appendices A–B retain the same components and procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use BDD-X and nuScenes-based DriveLM for the same driving tasks, and LISA for detector fine-tuning. No dataset, task, or distinct test scenario is added.

E2.justification: v2 adds TimeLLM to the BDD-X low-level control comparison in Table 3; v1 only discussed it as related work. Comparator membership in the high-level BDD-X and DriveLM comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, input histories, prediction horizons, metrics, model configuration, training budgets, and ablation settings remain unchanged. No separate new evaluation protocol is specified for the added TimeLLM row.

E4.justification: The component, PDCE-sigma, retrieval-K, environmental-predicate, predicate-selection, and rule-violation analyses are retained, as are the case studies. Several displays move from Appendix C into the main text without new analysis.

E5.justification: Benchmark and ablation results retain the same point-estimate reporting. Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the existing sampled prediction distributions are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds TimeLLM's speed/course RMSE values of 1.17/4.10 and corresponding tolerance accuracies. Previously reported values remain unchanged. TimeLLM becomes the strongest course-RMSE comparator, while SafeAuto remains best at 3.85.

T1.justification: The PDCE equation, MLN probability and inference definitions, retrieval similarity formulation, and appendix predicate sets, logical rules, and possible worlds are retained. No proof or mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The three contributions and headline claims concerning numerical accuracy, high-level prediction, and safety retain their scientific scope. The shortened abstract does not redefine these claims, and the introduction retains the same improvement percentages.

C2.justification: Interpretations of component effects and retrieval benefits remain unchanged, including the DriveLM rule-violation explanation. The limitations concerning PDCE distributions, predicate extraction, and retrieval filtering or reranking are also retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a SafeAuto code-repository link and availability statement in the abstract. Hardware, hyperparameters, processing instructions, prompts, and pseudocode otherwise remain unchanged; the link is an access disclosure, not verified repository contents.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds brief safety-guarantee framing citing Double Sampling Randomized Smoothing and DiffSmooth. TimeLLM was already cited in v1; its two bibliography entries in v2 represent the same work rather than distinct additions.

P1.justification: The abstract is condensed, affiliation/contact and publication information and acknowledgments are updated, and Section 5 and Appendix C are adjusted to reflect relocated ablations. Most scientific exposition remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v1 Tables 11–12 become main-text Tables 4–5, Table 10 becomes Table 6, and Figure 4 becomes Figure 3. Table 3 gains a baseline row, and appendix displays reflow. Existing graphics and table designs are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The added forecasting comparator, code-access disclosure, and placement of existing ablations alongside the main discussion modestly improve evaluation breadth and usability. A reporting inconsistency limits the gain: the retained 14.1% course-RMSE advantage over SOTA does not reflect the new TimeLLM comparator; Table 3 implies about 6.1% from 4.10 to 3.85. This affects the claimed margin, but preserves SafeAuto's leading course-RMSE ranking.
